q: What is a thrust block sized from?
o: Line pressure, pipe size and soil type
The depth of the trench only
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Pressure pushes on fittings where water changes direction. The block spreads that thrust into the soil.

q: In sizing water piping, what length is used?
o: The straight-line distance to the meter
The developed length to the most remote outlet
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Water piping is sized from the street-main pressure, the minimum pressure needed at fixtures, the height from meter to highest fixture, the developed length to the farthest outlet, and the total demand in water supply fixture units.

q: Where an atmospheric vacuum breaker protects a fixture, how high above its flood-level rim must it be?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: An atmospheric vacuum breaker only works if its critical level is at least 152 mm above the highest point water can reach downstream.

q: How is ferrous (iron or steel) water pipe protected where it is buried?
o: By laying it in dry sand only
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Soil moisture and chemicals corrode bare steel from the outside.

q: Where must a backflow preventer NOT be located?
o: Where toxic or corrosive fumes can reach it
Where it can be reached for testing
Above the ground in the open air
Near a shutoff valve on the line
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Atmospheric devices draw in air when they open, so fumes could be pulled into the water.

q: How often must backflow prevention assemblies be tested?
o: At least once a year, by a tester
Every five years, by the owner
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Springs and seals wear out. Yearly tests catch failed devices before contamination happens.

q: Why is lead limited in drinking-water pipe and fittings?
o: Lead leaches into the water and is toxic
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: The 1999 code capped lead at 8% in pipe and fittings. Modern lead-free standards allow far less, and solder at most 0.2%.

q: What must small cast iron fittings (51 mm and under) on potable water lines be?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Galvanizing keeps small iron fittings from rusting into the water.

q: Which of these is used in sizing water supply piping?
o: The pressure at the street main
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Water piping is sized from the street-main pressure, the minimum pressure needed at fixtures, the height from meter to highest fixture, the developed length to the farthest outlet, and the total demand in water supply fixture units.

q: What type of valve is used on water supply lines?
o: Full-way valves with non-corrosive working parts
Any valve, even with a narrow bore
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Full-way valves do not restrict flow when open.

q: Below what street pressure is the supply considered inadequate, calling for a booster system?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Below about 103 kPa at the fixtures, flush valves and showers do not work properly.

q: What is a water meter sized from?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: The meter must pass the peak demand without too much pressure loss.

q: What do beverage carbonators need on their water supply?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Carbon dioxide mixed with water is acidic and could flow back and dissolve copper into the supply.

q: What does a reduced-pressure principle assembly consist of?
o: One check valve and one air opening
Two checks with a relief valve between them
Two check valves with no relief valve
A single gate valve with test cocks
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Backflow devices: air gap (no device, just open space); atmospheric vacuum breaker (one body, one check, one air opening); pressure vacuum breaker (air inlet and check, testable); double check assembly (two checks); reduced-pressure assembly (two checks with a relief valve between).

q: What do water supply fixture units represent?
o: The amount of waste a fixture discharges
The number of fixtures in a room
The amount of water a fixture needs
The pipe size of a fixture
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Water supply fixture units add up to the demand used to size the pipes.

q: How often must vertical water piping be supported?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Supports at each floor keep the pipe's weight from resting on the lowest fittings.

q: What must hangers and straps on water piping NOT do?
o: Damage the pipe or stop it moving
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Pipes expand with heat. Tight or sharp supports damage them.

q: When a water pipe crosses a sewer, where must it be?
o: At least 0.30 m below the sewer
At least 0.30 m above the sewer
In the same trench, touching the sewer
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: A leaking sewer must not be able to seep into the water line.

q: What is the minimum size of a water service pipe?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Anything smaller cannot supply a typical dwelling at usable pressure.

q: How much clearance is needed between a backflow assembly and the floor or grade?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: The tester needs room to reach the test cocks, and relief discharge must not be blocked.

q: What is a mid-storey guide on a water riser for?
o: Keeping the vertical pipe in line
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Guides stop tall risers from bowing between floor supports.

q: What is the maximum setting of a water heater's pressure-relief valve?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Above this, a tank risks bursting.

q: How deep must water piping be buried?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Cover protects the pipe from damage and temperature swings.

q: What material is the body of a water supply valve 51 mm and smaller?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Brass resists corrosion. Larger valves may be cast iron or brass.

q: Above what static pressure must a pressure regulator be installed?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: High pressure causes water hammer, noise and leaking fixtures.

q: What screen covers water tank vents and overflows?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Screens keep insects and debris out of stored drinking water.

q: How are potable water outlets with hose threads protected?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: A hose left in a bucket or puddle could siphon dirty water back. An atmospheric vacuum breaker only works if its critical level is at least 152 mm above the highest point water can reach downstream.

q: How close must a union be to a water heater or other removable equipment?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: The union lets the equipment be taken out without cutting pipe.

q: Where are thrust blocks placed on water mains?
o: At tees, bends, dead ends and valves
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Thrust acts where water changes direction or stops.

q: How is buried copper water tube protected?
o: With a coat of paint only
With a coating, wrap or split casing
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Aggressive soils and cinders corrode copper.

q: What must a water storage tank have?
o: A sealed lid with no outlet
A valved drain and a screened overflow
An open top with no cover
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: The drain allows cleaning. The overflow stops the tank bursting if the float valve fails.

q: When may water piping be covered or concealed?
o: Only after the building is occupied
Only after it has been tested and inspected
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Leaks behind finished walls cost far more to fix.

q: Does plastic water pipe need wrapping against rust?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Only metal pipes rust. Plastic may still need protection from sunlight.

q: How are tanks, vats and pools filled from a potable line protected?
o: With a single check valve only
With a vacuum breaker 152 mm above the water
With a gate valve on the inlet
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: An atmospheric vacuum breaker only works if its critical level is at least 152 mm above the highest point water can reach downstream.

q: How is the pressure loss through a backflow preventer handled in design?
o: It is added to the street pressure
It is included in the pressure-loss calculation
It is subtracted from the fixture demand
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Reduced-pressure assemblies can drop 70 kPa or more.

q: What arrangement is prohibited in potable water piping?
o: Any that has a shutoff valve
Any that has more than one riser
Any that has a water meter
Any that lets polluted water into it
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: This is the basic cross-connection rule.

q: Which pressure figure matters in sizing water piping?
o: The minimum pressure needed at the fixtures
The pressure in the vent stack
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Water piping is sized from the street-main pressure, the minimum pressure needed at fixtures, the height from meter to highest fixture, the developed length to the farthest outlet, and the total demand in water supply fixture units.

q: Which height difference is used in sizing water piping?
o: From the roof to the ground
From the meter to the highest fixture
From the sewer to the meter
From the tank to the street
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Every metre of rise costs about 9.8 kPa of pressure. Water piping is sized from the street-main pressure, the minimum pressure needed at fixtures, the height from meter to highest fixture, the developed length to the farthest outlet, and the total demand in water supply fixture units.

q: What material may the body of a water supply valve larger than 51 mm be?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Large valves may use cast iron bodies with non-corrosive working parts.

q: What is required at every cross-connection?
o: A trap on the supply line
A vent on the supply line
A cleanout on the supply line
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Backflow devices: air gap (no device, just open space); atmospheric vacuum breaker (one body, one check, one air opening); pressure vacuum breaker (air inlet and check, testable); double check assembly (two checks); reduced-pressure assembly (two checks with a relief valve between).

q: How large must the vent of a gravity water tank be?
o: The same area as the downfeed riser
Half the area of the riser
Twice the area of the overflow
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Air must enter as fast as water leaves, or the tank will pull a vacuum.

q: How is potable water kept apart from another fluid in a heat exchanger?
o: With a double wall and a vented gap
With a check valve on the line
With a strainer on the inlet
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: If either wall fails, the leak shows at the vent instead of mixing the fluids.

q: What does an atmospheric vacuum breaker consist of?
o: Two check valves and a relief valve
One body, one checking member and one air opening
An air inlet and a check valve with test cocks
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Backflow devices: air gap (no device, just open space); atmospheric vacuum breaker (one body, one check, one air opening); pressure vacuum breaker (air inlet and check, testable); double check assembly (two checks); reduced-pressure assembly (two checks with a relief valve between).

q: How many kPa is 1 psi?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: So 80 psi is about 551 kPa, and 150 psi about 1,034 kPa.

q: What may be used where the supply pressure is too low?
o: A hydropneumatic tank or booster pump
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Pumps and tanks raise or store pressure. A reducing valve would only lower it further.

q: What stops a water tank from overflowing?
o: A check valve on the inlet
A float valve or level switch
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: The control shuts the inlet or pump off when the tank is full.

q: By convention, which side are hot and cold water outlets on a fixture?
o: Hot on the right, cold on the left
Hot on the left, cold on the right
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: The fixed convention prevents scalding when people reach for a tap.

q: Where is the vacuum breaker on a lawn sprinkler system?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: An atmospheric vacuum breaker must not be under constant pressure, so it goes after the control valve.

q: What must be true of shutoff valves on water lines?
o: They must be accessible at all times
They may be buried in walls
They may be locked in private rooms
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: In a leak, someone must reach the valve fast.

q: How must a relief-valve discharge pipe end?
o: Capped with a threaded plug at the end
Open, pointing down, 152 mm–0.60 m above ground
Into a closed pipe with a shutoff valve
Pointing up, above the roof line
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: The outlet must stay visible and open so scalding water cannot hit anyone and a stuck valve shows.

q: How close to a branch or change of direction must horizontal water piping be supported?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Fittings add weight and stress, so they need nearby support.

q: How are water-supplied aspirators protected?
o: With a trap on the outlet
With a vacuum breaker above the unit
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Aspirators create suction and could draw lab fluids into the water. An atmospheric vacuum breaker only works if its critical level is at least 152 mm above the highest point water can reach downstream.

q: Where must a backflow assembly installed high up have a platform?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: The tester needs a safe place to stand.

q: What does a pressure vacuum breaker consist of?
o: Two check valves and a relief valve
An air inlet and check valve, testable
One body and one air opening only
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Backflow devices: air gap (no device, just open space); atmospheric vacuum breaker (one body, one check, one air opening); pressure vacuum breaker (air inlet and check, testable); double check assembly (two checks); reduced-pressure assembly (two checks with a relief valve between).

q: What does a double check valve assembly consist of?
o: One check valve and one air opening
Two checks with a relief valve between
Two check valves with test cocks and shutoffs
A gate valve and a globe valve
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Backflow devices: air gap (no device, just open space); atmospheric vacuum breaker (one body, one check, one air opening); pressure vacuum breaker (air inlet and check, testable); double check assembly (two checks); reduced-pressure assembly (two checks with a relief valve between).

q: What does water-cooled equipment need on its supply?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Water in cooling equipment can be treated with chemicals.

q: For a flushometer's vacuum breaker, where must its critical level be?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: An atmospheric vacuum breaker only works if its critical level is at least 152 mm above the highest point water can reach downstream.

q: Which of these is NOT a listed water supply pipe material?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Clay is for gravity sewers, not pressure water lines.

q: What is the minimum air gap at a potable water outlet?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: It must also be at least twice the outlet diameter.

q: Which plastic pipe is suitable for both hot and cold water distribution?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: Chlorinated PVC takes hot water. Plain PVC softens with heat.

q: Where must a ball cock's critical level be in a flush tank?
o: 25 mm above the overflow pipe top
Below the top of the overflow pipe
At the bottom of the tank
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: If the tank overfills, water spills into the overflow long before it reaches the ball cock.

q: In branch sizing, what share of the cold and hot water demand is taken for a fixture with both?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 6
n: A fixture never draws full hot and full cold at once, so each branch is sized for 75% of the total.
